citation: 1834 S. Prairie. [The Fernando Jones house, John M. Van Osdel architect, 1866.] Unknown photographer, undated (before the mansard storey of 1886). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1834 S. Prairie; the Glessner House Museum's blog reproduces another print of the same negative ('John M. Van Osdel, Chicago's First Architect', 31 August 2015).
author: unknown photographer
date: undated (between 1866, when the house was built, and 1886, when the mansard storey it does not show was added)
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction; the original holder is not named). Prairie library images cgs-1834-jones-photo (this copy) and a18-gh-1834-fernando-jones (the Glessner House Museum blog's print of the same negative), both recorded there as 'link only'; the project's reference copies are the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/), committed since T-1888 at data/sources/assets/jones_1834_photos_t1888/ with their attribution, as the owner directed on 2026-10-11 for the image gate's pictures.
locator: The whole frame: the street front and, as the print stands, the flank on its left with a one-storey canted bay; the stoop, the lawn and the low stone wall before it; neighbouring houses at both edges. The print is laterally reversed (data/reference_views/jones_house_1834_prairie/chicagology_photo.json, its solve): turned back, the flank is the north one and the camera stands north-east of the house across Prairie Avenue.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-1888) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.

note: The one photograph of the Jones house this project builds from, before 1886. Turned the right way round it shows a two-storey Italianate house of dark brick over a high basement of smooth light ashlar: four opening columns on the front, the door in the second from the south at the head of a straight stoop of about eleven steps between scrolled cast-iron railings; every window and the door under a light segmental stone hood with a key and short ears; iron balconettes under the two north principal windows; round-headed basement lights under them; a deep cornice on paired carved brackets with panels between, over a plain frieze, round the front and the north flank; a low hipped roof with a broad centre gable over the front, an oculus in its tympanum; two tall stacks. On the north flank, a blank brick wall for some 6 m from the front corner, one window a storey, then a one-storey canted bay of light stone with a tall light in each face under a bracketed cornice, and over it a round-headed pair. A low stone wall stands on the street line before the lawn, with no fence on it.
what_it_supplies: the street front's composition: its four bays, the door's place, the window and door hoods, the balconettes, the basement lights, the stoop and its railings
the heights of the water table, the windows and the wall head through the photograph's camera
the north flank's windows and its canted bay
the bracketed cornice, and the low stone wall on the street line
